Learning Q-gram Distance

Posted by Riino on Friday, February 26, 2021

Some content of this article comes from the slide of Zsuzsanna Liptak.

Introduction

Q-gram, aka n-gram, is an algorithm to compare two strings with a given alphabet.

It is used in string retrieval with O(n)O(n)O(n) and a fixed static number qqq (in n-gram's case, this will be marked as nnn)

Definition of q-gram

q-gram is a string of length qqq, with a given alphabet Σ\SigmaΣ with length σ\sigmaσ.

For example, here we define :

Σ={′A′,′C′,′G′,′T′}\Sigma=\{'A','C','G','T'\}Σ={′A′,′C′,′G′,′T′}

thus σ=4\sigma = 4σ=4, if we define q=2q=2q=2, and we can choose q-grams from alphabet with a custom approach, like using lexicographic order.

Here we CAN select these strings over Σ\SigmaΣ :AA,AC,AG,AT,CA,CC,CG,CT,GA,GC,GG,GT,TA,TC,TG,TT

Definition of occurrence count

With an array of q-grams , we can define occurrence count with a given string sss:

N(s,q−gram)=∣{i:si…si+q−1}∣N(s,q-gram)=|\{i:s_i\dots s_{i+q-1}\}|N(s,q−gram)=∣{i:si​…si+q−1​}∣

e.g. Let sss = 'ACAGGGCA' and q=2q=2q=2, then N(s,AC)=N(s,AG)=N(s,GC)=1N(s,AC)=N(s,AG)=N(s,GC)=1N(s,AC)=N(s,AG)=N(s,GC)=1

In another word, NNN is the number of count that a g-gram figures in sss

Definition of q-gram table

With a axes of strings we want to compare, and another axes of q-grams, we can fill occurrence count into this matrix:

for sss= 'ACAGGGCA', ttt='GGGCAACA', vvv='AAGGACA', q-gram profiles = AA,AC,AG,AT,CA,CC,CG :

uuuPq(s)P_q(s)Pq​(s)Pq(t)P_q(t)Pq​(t)Pq(v)P_q(v)Pq​(v)
AA011
AC111

Definition of q-gram distance

For two strings sss and ttt, the q-gram distance is :

distq−gram(s,t)=∑u∈∑q∣N(s,u)−N(t,u)∣dist_{q-gram}(s,t)=\sum_{u\in\sum q}|N(s,u)-N(t,u)|distq−gram​(s,t)=u∈∑q∑​∣N(s,u)−N(t,u)∣

or equivalently:

distq−gram(s,t)=∑i=1σq∣Pq(s)[i]−Pq(t)[i]∣dist_{q-gram}(s,t)=\sum_{i=1}^{\sigma^q}|P_q(s)[i]-P_q(t)[i]|distq−gram​(s,t)=i=1∑σq​∣Pq​(s)[i]−Pq​(t)[i]∣

which is the Manhattan distance for two vectors ,which are the mapping result of given strings of q-gram profile

Algorithm

  • Use a sliding window of size qqq over sss and ttt
  • Use an array ddd of size σq\sigma^qσq, aka the q-gram profile
  • Scan s, then scan t, assign the occurrence count into ddd with different operators.
  • Now d[r]=N(s,ur)−N(t,ur)d[r]=N(s,u_r)-N(t,u_r)d[r]=N(s,ur​)−N(t,ur​)
  • Sum up the absolute value of ddd
def get_q_gram_distance(s,t,qgrams,q):
	n=len(s)
	m=len(t)
    d=[]
    for i in range(len(qgrams)):
        d.append(0)#init vector, O(q)

    for i in range(1,n-q+1):#slide window, O(n)
    	for r in range(0,len(grams)):#get count, O(q)
        	if s[i:i+q-1] == qgram[r]:
        		d[r]+=1#first vector sends postive effect


    for i in range(1,m-q+1):#slide window, O(m)
    	for r in range(0,len(grams)):#get count, O(q)
        	if s[i:i+q-1] == qgram[r]:
        		d[r]-=1#second vector sends negtive effect
    res=0
    for i in vector:
        res+=abs(i)

    return res

Tips:

  1. q-gram = 0 does not mean that two strings are same.
  2. distq−gram(s,t)2q<=dedit(s,t)\frac{dist_{q-gram}(s,t)}{2q}<=d_{edit}(s,t)2qdistq−gram​(s,t)​<=dedit​(s,t) , dedit(s,t)d_{edit}(s,t)dedit​(s,t) is the unit cost edit distance.
